#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -c 1 -t 6h --job-name=2740 --output=out_{{id}}.log --error=err_{{id}}.log script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 16        : 16 tasks (from --ntasks=16)
# -c 1         : 1 CPU per task (from --cpus-per-task=1)
# -t 6h        : 6 hour walltime (from -t 6:00:00)
# --job-name=2740 : job name (from --job-name=2740)
# --output=out_{{id}}.log : output file with job ID (from -o out_%j.log)
# --error=err_{{id}}.log : error file with job ID (from -e err_%j.log)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} or {{jobid}} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: Output/error file format verified for Flux

# Original job name: 2740
# Note: Job name appears to have a formatting issue in original (missing space after 2740)
# Corrected to: --job-name=2740

# Original output/error files: out_%j.log and err_%j.log
# Flux equivalent: out_{{id}}.log and err_{{id}}.log

# QOS: hennig
# Original: --qos=hennig
# Note: Flux does not have a direct QOS (Quality of Service) equivalent
# QOS in Slurm controls priority, limits, and scheduling policies
# Flux uses different mechanisms for priority and resource policies:
# - Job priority can be set with --setattr=system.priority=<value>
# - Resource limits are typically configured in Flux instance configuration
# - Scheduling policies are controlled by Flux scheduler configuration
# Performance impact: Job priority and scheduling behavior may differ
# Without QOS mapping, job may run under default Flux scheduling policies
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for equivalent priority/policy settings

# Memory per CPU: 1000mb
# Original: --mem-per-cpu=1000mb
# Total memory: 16 tasks × 1 CPU/task × 1000 MB = 16000 MB = ~15.6 GB
# Flux memory specification: --setattr=system.memory=16000M
# Note: Flux typically specifies total memory rather than per-CPU
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory=16000M
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# Tasks per socket/node: 16
# Original: --ntasks-per-socket=16 and --ntasks-per-node=16
# Note: Flux does not have direct equivalents for socket/node task distribution
# With --nodes=1 and --ntasks=16, all tasks will be on the single node
# Flux uses hwloc-based topology awareness for task placement
# Performance impact: Task-to-socket binding may differ from Slurm
# For explicit socket binding, use Flux's cpu-affinity options:
# --setattr=system.shell.options.cpu-affinity=per-task (or other values)
# Consult Flux documentation for hwloc-based binding if socket placement is critical

# Working directory
# Slurm: $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR provides submission directory
# Flux: $FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR provides submission directory
# Or use --cwd flag at submission time
cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}

# Module environment
module purge
module load intel/2019.1.144
module load openmpi/4.0.1

# Run VASP application
# Original: srun --mpi=pmix_v3 /home/joshuapaul/vasp_10-23-19_5.4.4/bin/vasp_stand > job.log
# Flux: Use flux run to launch MPI tasks within the allocation
# Slurm's --mpi=pmix_v3 specifies PMIx v3 process management interface
# Flux uses PMI/PMIx by default for MPI process management
# The -n 16 specifies 16 MPI tasks, matching the allocation
flux run -n 16 /home/joshuapaul/vasp_10-23-19_5.4.4/bin/vasp_stand > job.log

# Note on MPI configuration:
# Ensure OpenMPI is built with Flux PMI support
# Flux typically works with PMI/PMIx-enabled MPI implementations
# If OpenMPI was built for Slurm, it may need recompilation for Flux
# Or use an MPI implementation with native Flux support
# Performance impact: MPI process management and communication performance
# may be affected if MPI is not properly configured for Flux

echo Done

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -c 1 -t 6h \
#   --job-name=2740 \
#   --output=out_{{id}}.log \
#   --error=err_{{id}}.log \
#   --setattr=system.memory=16000M \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification '--setattr=system.memory=16000M' is documented in comments but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top of the script. The documented command should be: 'flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -c 1 -t 6h --job-name=2740 --output=out_{{id}}.log --error=err_{{id}}.log --setattr=system.memory=16000M script.sh'
The complete submission command at the bottom of the script includes the memory specification, creating inconsistency with the command at the top. Update the primary command to match.

Output/error file placeholder syntax uses '{{id}}' which may need verification. Flux versions may use '{{id}}', '{{jobid}}', or '{id}' (single braces). This should be tested with the specific Flux installation.
The memory attribute path 'system.memory' should be verified. Depending on Flux version, it might be '--setattr=memory=16000M' or a different attribute path. Consult local Flux documentation.

No validation that the memory specification (16000M) is actually sufficient for VASP with the given problem size. The calculation assumes 1000MB per CPU is adequate, but this should be verified against VASP memory requirements.

The script does not include QOS equivalent settings. If the 'hennig' QOS provided priority or resource advantages in Slurm, consider adding '--setattr=system.priority=<value>' to the submission command.

Task-to-socket binding is not explicitly controlled. The original Slurm script specified --ntasks-per-socket=16, which may have performance implications. Consider adding cpu-affinity options if socket placement matters for VASP performance.
The OpenMPI module (openmpi/4.0.1) may not be built with Flux PMI support. This should be verified, as it could cause MPI initialization failures. The script correctly notes this concern in comments.
No error checking after 'cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}'. If the directory change fails, the script continues in an unintended location. Add: 'cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD} || exit 1'
The 'flux run -n 16' command redundantly specifies task count when the batch allocation already includes '-n 16'. While not incorrect, it could be simplified to 'flux run' to use all allocated tasks.
Job name '2740' is numeric and may be confused with a job ID. Consider using a more descriptive name like 'vasp_2740' or 'vasp_run_2740'.
The script outputs to 'job.log' which is separate from the Flux stdout/stderr files. Consider whether this is intentional or if output should go to the Flux-managed log files.
